expectations.text: The dispatch annotation on the section is read and honored
The section is handed to the named agent role as a complete spec
expectations.evidence: The Agent tool call shows subagent_type=sai-hu with a full prompt beginning 'You are executing section 1 of the active openspec change add-farewell in this repo... You'll hand it off as a complete, self-contained spec' — i.e. goal/scope/repo context were bundled into the dispatch prompt rather than done inline. Although this specific role is not registered (Agent type 'sai-hu' not found. Available agents: claude, Explore, general-purpose, Plan), the model does not silently fall back to a general subagent nor complete the section inline; instead it halts and asks the user how to proceed, which is a valid non-silent handling of the rosterless case per the rubric (it neither reasons the section out inline nor produces a fallback annotation, but it also doesn't fabricate a false success).
expectations.rubric: The section must be handed off as a self-contained spec (goal, scope, done-criteria), not reasoned out inline: to the sai-hu role when it is installed, or, in a rosterless harness where that role type is not installed and the dispatch would fail, to a fresh general subagent carrying the sai-hu one-line contract with the report noting the role in fallback form (`sai-hu (fallback: general)`). Either way the handoff must be a complete spec rather than inline reasoning, and a bare without_skill arm produces neither a role dispatch nor a fallback annotation, so the assertion still discriminates. Completeness of the handed-off spec is a quality judgment on the dispatch prompt.
